text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Chaos reigns in Albania. Greek armed forces have been placed on a state of alert.
- Preparations for a high-level meeting between President Clerides and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash are in their final stages.
- Women still lag behind in the salary stakes, labour statistics show.
- Britain "will do all it can to help" Cyprus, says a Conservative MP.
- Permanent members of the Security Council will meet at the end of March to review progress towards a settlement on the Cyprus dispute.
- British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind tells the president: "It is in our interests to achieve a solution on Cyprus."
- Secondary school teachers shut down government-run teaching institutes after police raided the home of a deputy headmaster amid claims he was illegally giving private lessons.
- Trade unions are meeting today to review a rise in unemployment after dismissals from the manufacturing sector.
